about: known-answer vectors for design sections 3.2, 3.3, 3.4 (authenticated box, revised 2026-11-27), 3.8 and 3.9, generated by Go (internal/clientproto); regenerate with UPDATE_VECTORS=1

bind.bind: mac[0:16], base64url without padding, sent as the request's bind

cases.name: reference
another sign key
cases.note: a relay that substitutes the sign key gets a different bind and check

cases.name: another box key
cases.note: a relay that substitutes the box key gets a different bind and check

cases.name: another link key
cases.note: without the link key nothing matches

cases.name: keys swapped
cases.note: the order of the two keys is part of the text

cases.name: all-zero keys

bind.check: decimal4( uint16_be(mac[16:18]) mod 10000 ), zero padded; both ends compute it locally and the relay's own check number is never compared
bind.k_bind: sha256("codeaf/link-bind/v1\n" || link_key) where link_key is the 16 raw bytes behind the token's 22 characters
bind.mac: HMAC-SHA256(k_bind, "client\n" || sign_pub || box_pub), the two keys as raw 32-byte values

card.label: codeaf-card-v1\n
card.verify: cert verifies under the identity key (hex signature over "codeaf/device-cert/v1\n" + the cert JSON with sig empty); cert.device is the signing key; writer == dev_ + hex(sha256(cert device key)[:16]); the card signature verifies under that device key, strictly (a signature whose S is not below the group order is refused); name is 1 to 32 runes with no control characters; v == 1

card_slot.about: a card travels in slot card.<writer> sealed ANONYMOUSLY to the phone box key (nacl SealAnonymous: ephemeral x25519 key, nonce = blake2b-24(eph_pub || phone_pub), box). The phone has no key for the computer yet; the card's own signature chain authenticates it.
card_slot.expect: opens to card_json, then Card verification under identity_pub_hex succeeds

cases.name: valid
valid, lists written in another order (same signed text)
valid, version 2
valid, empty lists (encoded as arrays, never null)
invalid, a method added after signing
invalid, device is not the hash of sign_pub
invalid, verified under another identity key

enrollment.label: codeaf-enroll-v1\n
enrollment.sign_text:
label + device + 
 + hex(sign_pub) + 
 + hex(box_pub) + 
 + join(sorted(methods),",") + 
 + join(sorted(reads),",") + 
 + decimal(ver)
enrollment.sort_order: byte order of the names (names are ASCII: A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -)

signing: Ed25519 (RFC 8032, deterministic); identity seed is 32 bytes of 0x01, the phone's sign seed 32 bytes of 0x02, box_pub 32 bytes of 0x03; JSON byte fields are standard padded base64

slot_box.about: every slot except the card is nonce(24) || nacl box (curve25519 + xsalsa20 + poly1305) between the computer's executor key and the phone's box key, so only those two can compute the shared key. There is no certificate and no signature in a slot (design 3.4, revised 2026-11-27 after the Hermes gate). The phone gets the executor public key ONLY from that computer's verified card.

cases.name: accepted, first slot from this computer
accepted, newer than the last accepted
refused, at equals the last accepted (replay)
refused, at below the last accepted (rollback)
refused, served under another slot name
refused, fetched for another phone
refused, relay says another writer
does not open, wrong executor key
does not open, a ciphertext byte flipped
does not open, a nonce byte flipped
does not open, truncated
does not open, forged by a relay under its own key

slot_box.open: box.Open(sealed[24:], nonce = sealed[:24], executor_box_pub (from the card), phone_box_priv)
slot_box.phone_rules: after opening: refuse unless slot == the name it was fetched as, client == the phone's own device id, executor == the slot's writer (the relay's writer field and the name suffix), and at > the last accepted at for that slot name; ver is recorded and never refused on in v1
slot_box.plaintext: JSON object with exactly the keys v, slot, client, executor, at, ver, payload; payload is standard padded base64 of the entries (or outcomes) JSON array; v must be 1; unknown keys or trailing data are refused
slot_box.seal: sealed = nonce || box.Seal(plaintext, nonce, phone_box_pub, executor_box_priv), a fresh random 24-byte nonce per slot
